source_verification.title: Novel mutation in the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor (GNRHR) gene in a patient with normosmic isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Genetics of isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: role of GnRH receptor and other genes

second_answer_attack.resolution: A GnRH-neuron migration defect can cause hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, but it commonly impairs olfaction and acts upstream of the pituitary. Normal smell plus biallelic GNRHR loss and a blunted response to exogenous GnRH localize the defect to pituitary gonadotroph GnRH receptors.

blind_audit.rationale: GNRHR encodes the GnRH receptor on anterior pituitary gonadotrophs. Loss of receptor function prevents normal LH and FSH secretion in response to pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH, causing low sex steroids with low or inappropriately normal gonadotropins while olfaction remains intact. Strongest alternative resolved: A GnRH-neuron migration defect can cause hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, but it commonly impairs olfaction and acts upstream of the pituitary. Normal smell plus biallelic GNRHR loss and a blunted response to exogenous GnRH localize the defect to pituitary gonadotroph GnRH receptors.
